body: State Space Models (SSMs) have emerged as a compelling alternative to Transformers, enabling sequence modeling with constant memory and linear compute. Although SSMs exhibit reasonable performance and favorable computational characteristics, they continue to lag behind Transformers on tasks that require in-context learning and precise retrieval, slowing their adoption for large-scale language modeling. In this work, we demonstrate that both the success and failure of SSMs in these domains can be explained by studying the role of the gating mechanism, a prevalent component in modern recurrent networks. Specifically, we show through theory and experiments that this gating mechanism causes SSMs to first learn an in-weights "memorization" solution, while delaying, or even preventing, convergence to a correct in-context learning solution. Importantly, this happens even in cases where there are no fundamental limitations due to the architecture or its memory capacity. On the other hand, we find that gating is often beneficial for improving generalization to long sequence lengths. Our results illuminate the crucial role of the gating mechanism in shaping both the training dynamics and generalization of SSMs, and provide a basis for understanding and improving linear-time models.
summaryZh: 本文分析了状态空间模型（SSM）在上下文学习（ICL）和精确检索任务上落后于Transformer的原因。研究发现，SSM中的门控机制虽然有助于长序列泛化，但会导致模型优先学习“权重内记忆”方案，从而延迟或阻碍其收敛到正确的上下文学习解。通过理论与实验，作者揭示了门控机制在塑造训练动态中的关键作用，为改进线性时间复杂度模型提供了重要的架构设计参考。

glossary.explanationZh: 状态空间模型，一种具有线性计算复杂度的序列建模架构。
门控机制，用于控制信息流动的神经网络组件。
上下文学习，模型在不更新权重的情况下通过提示词学习新任务的能力。
记忆化，指模型通过参数存储特定训练数据而非泛化推理。
